analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/threat-model-review.md. It documents CI threat-review tooling (workload call policy, 500-call emergency ceiling, 16,384 output tokens, 50-minute scan timeout, removal of manual paid depth dispatch, depth_policy.py routing). It touches no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption or cache code, so it has no direct effect on the canonical threat-model assets (A-001..A-017) or on TB-002/003/007/009/010/011 and T-041.

I examined the head text against the base text for claims that weaken a security posture.
- Manual paid dispatch is removed (head lines 79-86). Dispatch is limited to the unpaid preflight, so paid-spend and abuse surface shrinks. PR text and labels still cannot request spend.
- Scanner code still comes from the trusted default branch, and the threat model is still read as data from the base SHA. PR head code is never executed (head lines 82-86).
- The documented fork policy keeps forks on the capped OpenRouter route unless BEDROCK_SCAN_ALLOW_FORKS=true is set (head lines 166-168). The manual-dispatch exception for forks is removed, which is consistent with removing manual dispatch.
- Documented routing heuristics (head lines 377-393) send workflows and critical paths to Sol and let docs/tests skip Opus. Sonnet still covers every unit, and findings or uncertainty still escalate. The doc explicitly calls these routing heuristics, not proof of safety.
- Human-review handoff, clearance and membership policy (head lines 217-235) are not weakened. Head line 233 is tightened: after a member is removed, require independent human review.
- The workload call ceiling and 600-second timeout raise potential AWS spend (the doc notes there is no dollar cap). That is a documented operational tradeoff in a docs-only change, not a security regression.

Open question for integration, not a finding: the actual workflow, depth_policy.py and budget_scan.py implementations are not in this batch, so I cannot verify that they match the documented behavior (for example, that manual dispatch really does not start paid work). Any security conclusion about that depends on those unseen files.
